To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a construction technique for resilient (n,m)-bit S-boxes with SAO nonlinearity and higher dimension m > bn4c.
we have constructed a resilient S-box with SAO nonlinearity for m = 4n/3−2n/3− 2n−3/3−1/3 and n ≥ 3.
we provide the first construction technique for resilient S-box design with higher-dimensional output spaces and extremely high nonlineary.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following two main issues.
the design of resilient S-boxes that are suitable for cryptographic applications.
the construction of resilient S-boxes of dimension (n,m) with n > 4, m > 2, and m ≤ n− 1, where n is a power of two and m is a multiple of four.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our construction is the first one that provides a systematic way to construct SAO resilient S-boxes for a larger output space than previously known.
we have provided the first construction technique for resilient S-box with SAO nonlinearity for m > bn2 c.
our new method is the first construction technique for resilient S-box design that allows the construction of S-boxes for m > bn3 c, where the nonlinearity is strictly almost optimal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the construction technique proposed here is a very efficient way of obtaining resilient S-boxes of higher dimensions and with higher nonlinearities.
the proposed S-boxes are the best resilient S-boxes known to date in terms of the number of the output bits and the nonlinearity.
the proposed method is a generalization of the construction technique for resilient S-box design proposed by Zheng, Matsumoto, and Imai.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a GMM type construction can be used to construct resilient S-boxes that have higher-dimensional vectorial output.

the GMM technique, which is based on generalized Maiorana-McFarland (GMM) S-boxes and has previously been successfully used for resilient (n,m)-S-boxes with m ≤ 2n/3, can be extended to the case where m > 2n/4.
the proposed construction technique is very flexible, and it can be applied to a wide range of parameters.
